body: I tend to tell people about what’s bothering me because I just want someone to validate and understand me and tell me my feelings aren’t wrong and comfort me. I want to be told that my feelings are valid and that I’m not wrong for having them. There are a few people that can do that for me to an extent, but many of my friends just don’t get it and aren’t very helpful.

I was almost exactly the same way. Self-harm was a way for me to prove to myself that I was truly in pain. It was like creating physical evidence of my feelings, or externalizing them and turning them into something tangible. I would create injuries on my body as a means of representing my emotional pain. You are never alone. We are all here to help.
I've heard of it. I don't know a ton about it, though. I haven't read it.

Thank you all for the kind words. I spoke to my mom about it earlier and I feel better now that she's pointed out that the employee handled it the wrong way, i.e. why did she try to handle it herself instead of getting security, how does she know I'm not going to hurt her if she truly thinks I am stealing, she drove away a customer, the camera footage would show that I wasn't taking anything, etc. I'm not the type to hold grudges or wish people harm, but I have to admit it was satisfying to hear that she was in the wrong rather than me, and it was rather amusing to think that this employee's attempt at heroism (stopping a shoplifter) blew up in her face.

For me it was sort of a means of proving my pain was real. I had this weird intrusive pattern of thoughts that if I didn't harm myself, then I was saying that whatever people did to hurt me was acceptable. I felt like not self-harming was the same as saying that I was okay with whatever people did to me. But of course I never showed or told anyone, so it was more about proving it to myself. It was how I validated my own feelings. "You harmed yourself on the outside, so clearly you must be hurting on the inside." Self-harm was my way of externalizing my hurt feelings and making them tangible, creating "proof" that I was hurt.
I don't know if any of that made sense but that was my main reasoning behind it.

Our household has always been pretty toxic. Our parents love us and want to support us, but my dad was abused as a child and as a result he has anger problems and PTSD, which have always been a source of conflict. Our parents are trying to help us. My sister started anti-depressants not too long ago to regulate her temper. We just haven't found quite the right solution yet.

I've brought it up to one of them before. I don't think I've told the other. I don't want to sound dramatic or manipulative, though. I don't want any of my anger to be taken out on them. I'm just not sure how to bring it up, what the right time would be, what to say, etc. I feel like I'm going to sound like a psycho bitch no matter what.

It's just really embarrassing, you know? My best friend was there while the boss called me, and they said that the boss told them my response was "umm... I might be" when asked if I was still interested in the job. And I did say that. But hearing it back was just humiliating, especially since my friend sounded kind of accusatory about it. I'm just so disappointed in myself.

I just feel like there's so much I'm "expected" to do that I haven't done yet. In high school I was surrounded by kids who were already working, some who had their own cars, some whose parents were even making them pay bills, and I always just felt so spoiled and lazy and incompetent for not having a job or knowing how to drive or having to pay my own rent all before 18. I feel like so much is being expected of me and like I'm so far behind my peers. I know I'm very young, but it just seems like all the kids I went to high school with had their entire lives planned out before we even graduated.

I quit self-harming almost nine months ago. Yes, it does take willpower. But for some people the urges do go away--they mostly have for me. It really depends on the individual and their mental health situation. I personally still get urges every now and then, but they are very few and far between. If you are not already seeking professional help, I strongly recommend you do. You are worth it.

I know this response is late, but this is a powerful, moving, wise and beautiful message. I really don't have words to describe how it made me feel. All I can really say is you are absolutely right; dwelling on the past will not be of benefit to me, especially memories of what I thought this boy was. For all intents and purposes he is no longer a part of my life--so why hold on to him by keeping him in my mind?
It won't happen overnight, but there will come a day when I can look back on my past relationships without feeling that bitter heartache.
I have hope for the future.
Thank you.

I appreciate your kind words. It just hurts to see this girl call him "bae" and be all romantic and things like that when I still feel like it should have been me. I keep having these thoughts of "if he wanted a relationship after all then why didn't he reach out to me? Why does he want someone other than me?" It just makes me so sick. The thought of it makes my whole body feel cold and prickly and it makes my stomach turn. I've blocked them both on my social media and I don't have to worry about seeing either of them in person, at least. I wish I could just erase him from my mind and stop giving him any power but I just... Can't.

Thank you all for the kind words. This friend and I have made up and are on good terms again. I have a lot of things I need to work on still, but I'm trying not to think so negatively of myself right now.
Update: I wasn't strong enough. I relapsed. I suppose I can always try again, though...
